section_1_treasury_approval_criteria.summary: DReps apply a multi-factor evaluation framework when deciding on treasury spending. The criteria cluster around five core themes.

transparency_and_cost_breakdown.description: The single most cited reason for NO votes. DReps routinely reject proposals that offer lump-sum asks without itemized cost breakdowns.
evidence: Cardanians on Cardano Critical Integrations Budget: 'There is no itemized cost breakdown, no clear prioritization of integrations, and limited visibility into partner selection or execution strategy. This level of opacity is not acceptable for the largest budget request in Cardano's history.'
Talos on Critical Integrations: 'Missing justification – The proposal lists a single lump sum without a granular breakdown or cost-justification for each integration.'
GAIA on Intersect MBO: 'There is an overall lack of transparency regarding the final budget total and where that money is being spent.'

accountability_and_milestones.description: DReps want specific, measurable deliverables with enforcement mechanisms. Vague KPIs trigger skepticism.
evidence: Maureen on IO Engineering: 'Where are the KPIs and deliverables on each line item? This feels like the classic big tech company approach of throwing money at problems until they go away.'
TriangleForces on IO Engineering: 'I vote YES - provided full transparency, milestone enforcement and aggressive public reporting of progress and spend.'

Cardanians on Summit 2026: 'The proposal lists many KPI categories, but it does not translate them into hard, measurable commitments (with baselines, targets, tracking method, and post-event reporting) that justify an ask of this size.'

constitutionality.description: Multiple DReps explicitly check Article IV requirements. Unconstitutional proposals trigger NO even when the substance is meritworthy.
evidence: GAIA on Snek Global Listing: 'Article IV Section 3: The proposal does not appear to be part of an approved Cardano ecosystem budget. Article IV Section 4: No allocation is made for independent audits. Article IV Section 5: The proposal does not specify that the receiving wallet is undelegated.'
InputEndorsers on Snek: 'This proposals has requested just 5ADA in the field for the withdrawal amount... I have to presume it is a likely typo. Hence, I vote NO.'

net_change_limit_ncl_compliance.description: Several DReps maintain personal NCL thresholds and vote NO when cumulative spending exceeds their limit.
evidence: GAIA on Critical Integrations: 'This amount surpasses my personal NCL for 2025, and there are no good reasons for me to vote yes despite this.'
GAIA on 275M Budget: 'This budget surpasses my personal NCL of 250M ADA.'
TriangleForces: 'We must first establish how much the treasury can sustainably allocate without compromising network health, then apply stringent selectivity to proposals.'

public_goods_test.description: DReps distinguish between public goods (infrastructure, open-source tools, governance) and commercial products. Commercial proposals face much higher scrutiny.
evidence: InputEndorsers: 'Treasury funds should primarily be focused on critical public goods in different forms. Especially if they are open source; support infrastructure, research, tools, even education, promotion of Cardano.'

GAIA on DeFi Liquidity Budget: 'I don't think providing liquidity to DeFi operations should be funded from treasury ADA. DeFi operations have to be self-sustaining as they are completely a commercial product.'
InputEndorsers on Pogun: 'The Treasury should be very careful about stepping into markets where private capital, users and product-market fit should normally decide winners.'

track_record_and_team_credibility.description: Established teams with prior Cardano contributions receive more benefit of the doubt. New or unproven teams face steeper scrutiny.
evidence: InputEndorsers on DeFi Withdrawal 1: '[Elder Millenial] has built SteelSwap - a Cardano DApp (no token!) that I have used most frequently over the years. This also makes me aware that the proposer does have significantly more extensive experience with Cardano DeFi.'

EMURGO on Snek: 'The Snek team has demonstrated exceptional execution capability, securing Tier 1 listings through self-funding and driving unmatched adoption for a Cardano native token. These achievements are commendable and recognized.'

section_2_io_proposals.summary: IO proposals show the most nuanced treatment — widely considered essential yet criticized for lack of granularity. The 96M ADA engineering withdrawal passed with near-unanimous YES votes but generated extensive commentary demanding better accountability.

IO Core Engineering (96.8M ADA).pattern: Overwhelmingly YES (~90%) with few NOs (Cardano Whale, Homer J, Maureen, drep1yf6x...) and notable Abstains (Cardano Foundation, DraculaDAO, Agora, Cardanians)
IO Core Engineering (96.8M ADA).cf_reasoning: CF abstained due to 'lack of sufficient transparency or accountability'; 'scope, cost-effectiveness, and safeguards not adequately addressed after community feedback'
IO Core Engineering (96.8M ADA).yes_reasoning: Considered essential 'core engineering to keep the lights on'; IO's track record in building Cardano foundation earns trust
IO Core Engineering (96.8M ADA).no_reasoning: Maureen: '97 million ADA for what reads like a university research department's wishlist'; no KPIs per line item; too many simultaneous priorities

IO Research (26.8M ADA).pattern: CF Abstained citing 'key components materially too high'; others largely YES following budget process alignment
IO Research (26.8M ADA).trust_level: High baseline trust in IO research capability but concerns about cost and scope expansion

IO Catalyst (69.4M ADA).pattern: CF voted YES: 'important to ensure continuity for the main source of grant funding during a transition year'
IO Catalyst (69.4M ADA).general_view: Catalyst continuation widely supported as a known, tested funding mechanism

IO modular initiatives (Consensus, Dev E.pattern: Strong YES consensus. Modular breakdown actually improved DRep confidence vs. single large ask
IO modular initiatives (Consensus, Dev E.key_insight: Breaking IO work into named sub-initiatives (Leios, Consensus, DevEx) was viewed positively — gave DReps something concrete to evaluate

key_themes: IO is given significant benefit of the doubt due to foundational contributions, but this trust is conditional on transparency

TriangleForces conditional YES: 'It will not be a black box or IOE slush fund. We need to see exactly what is being delivered for every ADA spent. If Intersect do not enforce this, I will not give them my vote next year.'
The 96M ask was the single largest withdrawal; its near-universal passage confirms IO retains strong DRep trust for core engineering
CF's abstention on IO Engineering was a notable signal — even the organization's closest ally had transparency concerns
Concern about dependency: IO currently irreplaceable, creating governance risk
section_2_io_proposals.amount_sensitivity: DReps accept large IO amounts when framed as essential infrastructure. The 96M passed; the 70M Critical Integrations had more friction due to confidentiality.

section_3_defi_liquidity.summary: The DeFi liquidity proposals represent the most ideologically divided category. A core set of DReps who accept the 50M ADA DeFi budget (as treasury-deployed liquidity that can generate returns) clash with those who see it as improperly subsidizing commercial ventures.

Cardano Treasury DeFi Liquidity Budget (.result: Overwhelmingly NO — nearly every DRep voted NO or Abstain. This version failed.
key_no_reasons: GAIA: 'DeFi operations have to be self-sustaining as they are completely a commercial product'
Cerkoryn: '50M ADA ask plus relatively high management stipends feels oversized; would prefer a smaller pilot'
Almost universal opposition: $Khale, 42, Agora, AKYO, Cardano Foundation, Cardano Whale, CardanoYoda, Christopher Erckert, Chris Cata, Ha-Nguyen, HeptaSean, all voted NO

Cardano DeFi Liquidity Budget - Withdraw.result: Mixed — roughly 55% YES, 30% NO, 15% Abstain after a revised, staged approach
Cardano DeFi Liquidity Budget - Withdraw.shift_from_original: The shift to a 'pilot/staged' model changed many votes
key_yes_reasons: Cerkoryn: 'This is not a spend by the treasury, this is a managed fund that has the potential to generate returns for the treasury, making it inherently an EV-positive play (minus risk).'
Cardano Foundation: 'Requesting a smaller initial tranche to establish necessary legal and technical guardrails before managing a 50M ADA budget is a responsible approach.'
GAIA: Simply followed through from earlier budget approval vote
key_no_reasons: Cardanians: 'I voted YES on the overall 50M ADA DeFi liquidity direction. This NO is about Withdrawal 1 — unnamed directors, estimated fees, unaddressed COI'
TriangleForces: 'Sundae Labs asks the treasury to finance pre-deployment overhead before proving constitutional clarity, genuine necessity, and superiority over lower-cost alternatives'

Stablecoin DeFi Liquidity Budget.pattern: Similar split; stablecoin-specific framing gets somewhat more support than generic DeFi
Stablecoin DeFi Liquidity Budget.note: Stablecoins viewed as critical infrastructure (unlike general DeFi), improving acceptance

Cardano x Draper Dragon Orion Fund (50M.key_differentiator: VC fund structure with treasury-first repayment model before GP profits was seen as a key safeguard
Cardano x Draper Dragon Orion Fund (50M.cerkoryn_analysis: 'The decision to pay back the treasury FIRST before the GP makes any profit is the saving grace to this proposal.'
Cardano x Draper Dragon Orion Fund (50M.gaia_no_reasoning: 'No investment capital being allocated by Tim Draper/Draper Dragon... entirely no risk to the Draper entities. Huge upside for Draper with all the risk from the Cardano community.'

core_ideological_divide.pro_defi_view: Treasury ADA is idle capital; DeFi liquidity provision can generate returns and deepen ecosystem while the capital is ultimately returned. It's an investment, not a spend.
core_ideological_divide.anti_defi_view: DeFi is commercial; private capital should decide DeFi winners. Treasury subsidizing liquidity distorts markets, creates precedent, and puts public funds at commercial risk without genuine accountability.
core_ideological_divide.swing_factor: The presence of a treasury-first repayment mechanism, independent audits, and staged disbursement converts many NO to YES votes

section_4_events_marketing.summary: Events and marketing proposals face intense scrutiny with a strong tendency toward NO votes, particularly when: (1) amounts are large, (2) founding entities are the primary administrators, (3) KPIs are soft, (4) there is bundling of multiple events.

Cardano Summit 2026 + TOKEN2049 (14M ADA.result: Overwhelming NO (~75%) with some Abstains from entities with COI concerns
Cardano Summit 2026 + TOKEN2049 (14M ADA.cardano_foundation_vote: Abstain — CF abstained because a revised version was submitted on-chain simultaneously
key_no_reasons: GAIA: 'Hell no! After last year's Cardano Summit fiasco where the community was exploited with abusive ticket prices...'

TriangleForces: 'Treasury money is not marketing pocket money, and prestige is not a public good! When the pitch depends on foot traffic, audience scale, and industry buzz, I start hearing FOMO dressed up as strategy.'

InputEndorsers: 'The requested scale is substantial: $2.5M for the Summit and $1.16M for TOKEN2049. I also have a standing platform commitment to vote NO on EMURGO-related treasury withdrawals until March 15, 2027.'
Cardanians: 'Bundled package, no granularity... sustainability is not demonstrated... KPIs are too soft for the spend'
Cardano Summit 2026 + TOKEN2049 (14M ADA.cf_concern: CF disclosed COI as organizer and deferred to the revised proposal

Cardano Summit 2025 (6M ADA, Withdraw).result: CF voted YES; part of the Intersect budget package. Generally accepted as part of broader budget.
Cardano Summit 2025 (6M ADA, Withdraw).contrast: The 2025 Summit was absorbed into the Intersect budget process with less controversy than the standalone 2026 Summit ask

Pavilions at Exhibitions (889K ADA).result: CF adjusted from NO to YES after scope revised; generally accepted at lower amount
Pavilions at Exhibitions (889K ADA).threshold_observation: Sub-1M marketing spends with clear scope revision attract YES; multi-million standalone asks do not

threshold_triggers.concern_level_low: Under 1M ADA with clear deliverables and revised scope
threshold_triggers.concern_level_medium: 1M-6M ADA; accepted if part of Intersect budget process with community oversight
threshold_triggers.concern_level_high: Over 6M ADA as standalone event/marketing; triggers deep scrutiny and likely NO
automatic_rejection_signals: Bundling multiple events in one withdrawal without separate line-item votes
Founding entity (CF/EMURGO) as primary proposer and beneficiary
Soft KPIs (reach, buzz, impressions) without hard adoption outcomes
Year-over-year budget increases rather than sustainability pathway
Submitted outside Intersect budget process ('reduces comparability vs. other marketing requests')

section_4_events_marketing.notable_quote: TriangleForces: 'This proposal reeks of kindergarten-level thinking: shouting loudest in the biggest room instead of whispering strategically in the right ears.'

section_5_exchange_listings.summary: The Snek/exchange listing proposals generated almost universal NO votes, making them among the most decisively rejected proposals in the dataset. The rejection was based on a combination of constitutional defects, missing repayment mechanisms, and the single-token-benefit concern.

Cardano Global Listing Expansion - Power.result: Overwhelming NO (~90%). Only a handful of YES (Maureen, Rod G, SureWealthNG). Several Abstains.
Cardano Global Listing Expansion - Power.emurgo_vote: NO — 'treasury allocations for exchange listings should be tied to clear, measurable benefits for the broader ecosystem, either through collective infrastructure, demonstrable long-term ROI, or repayment to the Treasury'

Withdraw 5M for Cardano's Global Listing.technical_defect: InputEndorsers: 'This proposal has requested just 5ADA in the field for the withdrawal amount — I have to presume it is a likely typo. Hence, I vote NO.'

Withdraw 3.1M for Ecosystem Exchange Lis.result: CF voted YES 'in line with the GMC's voting and according to previous viability assessments.' Generally accepted as part of Intersect package.
Withdraw 3.1M for Ecosystem Exchange Lis.contrast: Ecosystem-wide listing service with oversight passed; single-token listing without oversight failed decisively

key_arguments_against_snek: Cerkoryn: 'I find a 5M ADA ask to support SNEK listing on exchanges to be a bit too much. Our focus should really be on stablecoin liquidity and exchange listings more than any other CNT.'

GAIA: 'I would expect 5 Million ADA would get us multiple CNT listings for a variety of tokens, not just SNEK. I'd expect some kind of repayment plan or community compensation plan in exchange for the ADA given.'

EMURGO: 'This proposal focuses on a single-token listing without [collective infrastructure, demonstrable long-term ROI, or repayment] mechanisms, creating a precedent that may be difficult to sustain.'
Constitutional problems: Not part of approved budget; no independent audit allocation; receiving wallet not designated as undelegated
what_would_pass: Ecosystem-wide listing mechanism covering multiple CNTs
Clear repayment mechanism or treasury revenue share
Part of an approved Intersect budget process
Hard KPIs tied to measurable ecosystem-wide outcomes
section_5_exchange_listings.broader_exchange_listing_view: DReps are not opposed to exchange listings per se — the 3.1M ecosystem listing service (administered by Intersect) received YES votes including CF. The objection to Snek was the single-token benefit, missing accountability, and unconstitutional structure.

section_6_intersect.summary: Intersect occupies an ambiguous position — viewed as necessary infrastructure for budget administration but criticized for opacity, centralization tendencies, and the tension between being 'member-based' while seeking full community funding.

Intersect MBO 15.75M ADA.result: Majority YES (~65%) but with significant NO bloc (~20%) and some Abstains
Intersect MBO 15.75M ADA.cf_vote: YES — acknowledged revised budget, recognized Intersect's shift toward leaner operations
Intersect MBO 15.75M ADA.emurgo_vote: YES — 'necessary and constructive step toward sustainable treasury allocation'
key_yes_reasons: InputEndorsers: 'A lot of proposals are now dependent on the presence of a rational and functional administrator... Jack Briggs and his communication skills and responsive style — yep, it matters... Intersect cut the treasury withdrawal from the massive 20M ADA... [They] avoided the massive temptation of bundling all proposals into 1 or 2 TW.'
InputEndorsers: 'I want to reciprocate with my own leap of faith, by supporting a key cog in the system — the new community-minded Intersect.'
key_no_reasons: GAIA: 'Intersect wants to operate as an MBO with all the benefits of being an MBO (board of directors, answering only to members), but then they want to be completely community funded. You cannot have this both ways.'
Cardanians: '₳15,750,000 is a massive budget request — enough to fund a 150-person company for a year — yet the proposal lacks a detailed cost structure, staffing plan, or milestones.'

TriangleForces: 'The governance and oversight model remains heavily centralized around Intersect's leadership. This concentration raises risks of operational bottlenecks and insufficient decentralization.'
Multiple DReps: Cardano's three founding entities have ample resources via genesis ADA to fund an organization like Intersect if they believe in its strategic necessity

Cardano Builder DAO (12M ADA).result: CF YES: 'mitigates the dependency of Cardano on grants by exploring convertible grants'
Cardano Builder DAO (12M ADA).general_reception: More positively received than Intersect operational budget — seen as funding innovation rather than administration

Budget Process Framework.result: Cerkoryn YES: 'substantial improvement from last year'; praised modular Work Packages, 67% Ekklesia threshold, Strategic Pillars linked to ecosystem KPIs

trust_assessment.trustees_view: Intersect is the least-trusted founding entity for large operational budgets but increasingly trusted as a technical administrator after leadership changes and budget cuts
trust_assessment.reform_recognition: Multiple DReps explicitly praised the leadership change (Jack Briggs), the reduction from 20M to 15.75M, and the refusal to bundle all proposals
persistent_concerns: Insufficient transparency in personnel costs and role definitions
Tension between 'member-based' structure and community-funded mandate
Board Services cost ($250K) separate from and on top of director compensation ($35K/director)
trust_assessment.centralization_risk_flag: DReps consistently flag that an organization meant to facilitate decentralization should not itself be a centralization point

section_6_intersect.intersect_vs_other_mbos: Intersect receives more scrutiny than individual tool teams because it controls the administrative pipeline. Approving Intersect operationally means trusting it to administer ~275M ADA in withdrawals — a different risk profile than approving a single developer tool.

section_7_small_vs_large.summary: Small withdrawals (under ~500K ADA) for established developer tools receive near-unanimous YES votes with minimal deliberation. Large withdrawals trigger extensive debate and higher rejection rates.

BloxBean Java Tools (99.6K ADA).deliberation: Minimal — most rationales are very short confirmations
BloxBean Java Tools (99.6K ADA).no_reasons: brock: Blanket position against some proposals; not specific to BloxBean

Lucid Evolution (130.9K ADA).result: CF Abstained on this and several similar small tools (alignment concerns)

OpShin (199.9K ADA).result: CF Abstained on financial mechanics concerns

Dolos (220.9K ADA).result: CF YES — clear alignment with infrastructure principles

Scalus (657.7K ADA).result: CF YES — alignment with DApps platform strategy

section_7_small_vs_large.key_finding: Small withdrawals (under ~500K) for established open-source developer tools are essentially 'waved through' by most DReps. The few NOs are typically from DReps with blanket voting positions, not specific objections to the proposal. The exception is CF, which applies a structured evaluation framework even to small proposals.

size_thresholds.under_500k: Near automatic YES if open-source developer tooling with prior community use. Scrutiny minimal.
size_thresholds.500k_to_3M: Moderate scrutiny; team track record becomes important; some pushback on cost justification
size_thresholds.3M_to_15M: Significant scrutiny; requires clear deliverables, accountability mechanisms, and community benefit beyond the proposer
size_thresholds.over_15M: High scrutiny; expected to be part of Intersect budget process; unconstitutionality concerns; NCL considerations; requires extraordinary justification
size_thresholds.over_50M: The most contested zone. IO Engineering (96M) passed with near-consensus due to recognized necessity. DeFi Liquidity (50M) narrowly passed only in staged form. Critical Integrations (70M) passed despite significant opposition.

section_7_small_vs_large.note_on_equal_scrutiny: Despite size differences, the Cardano Foundation applies equal constitutional scrutiny to all proposals — abstaining on small proposals where financial mechanics are unclear. This creates an interesting divide: most DReps wave through small tools, while CF votes with equal rigor across all sizes.

section_8_no_vote_triggers.summary: Analysis of consistent NO vote patterns across the dataset reveals seven primary trigger conditions.

triggers.quote: Cardanians: 'This level of opacity is not acceptable for the largest budget request in Cardano's history.'
Dave: 'Bundling 39 proposals into a single vote is misleading, non-transparent, and enables manipulation. It forces DReps into a binary, all-or-nothing choice.'
GAIA on Snek: 'Article IV Section 4: No allocation is made for independent audits or defined oversight mechanisms. This is a requirement.'

triggers.trigger: Founding entity funding for own operations/events
triggers.quote: GAIA: 'The Cardano Foundation and EMURGO should be using genesis ADA to pay for building Cardano, not exploiting the treasury every week or two.'
InputEndorsers on Pogun: 'I am still not comfortable with the Treasury funding commercial products directly on these terms. This can tilt competition toward one team, distort the market.'
Dave: 'The proposal relies on unverifiable off-chain metrics... Without on-chain data, such figures cannot be independently verified or trusted.'
GAIA: 'This surpasses my personal NCL of 250M ADA. Omnibus budgets are the only way skewed results like this are able to circumvent intended on-chain guardrails.'

triggers.trigger: Soft/vanity KPIs without measurable adoption outcomes
triggers.quote: TriangleForces on Summit: 'The value proposition is: we need to be seen at a very big event because important people will be there. I find that strategically weak.'
Cardanians on Summit: 'The proposal is submitted outside the Intersect budget process due to timing, which reduces comparability versus other marketing requests.'
Talos: 'The spending plan is wrapped in confidentiality, meaning the community can't see how the money will be allocated or audited. That opacity undermines trust.'

section_9_notable_quotes.quote: Weren't these things the responsibility of the founding entities to use their genesis ADA to pay for and get done? Also yes. Why aren't EMURGO and the Cardano Foundation paying for this infrastructure since it is their financial responsibility as part of their role? They would much rather make ADA holders pay, and keep their genesis ADA to continue to influence governance.
section_9_notable_quotes.significance: Captures the fundamental tension between founding entity responsibilities and community treasury use

section_9_notable_quotes.quote: This proposal reeks of kindergarten-level thinking: shouting loudest in the biggest room instead of whispering strategically in the right ears. Cardano's time and budget deserve better than a scattergun approach masquerading as ambition.
section_9_notable_quotes.significance: Articulates a sophisticated critique of the events/marketing approach that resonates with many DReps

section_9_notable_quotes.quote: In a still nascent blockchain economy, spending more essentially means converting the native token for fiat, and the result is devaluation. We are not exchanging ADA directly for Cardano economy goods and services, we are selling it into the real world. The ADA is not recycled internally. This adds downward pressure on ADA's price.
section_9_notable_quotes.significance: The most sophisticated economic analysis of treasury spending effects in the dataset

section_9_notable_quotes.quote: Our yes vote is a pragmatic decision to ensure that the crucial step of establishing a budget is taken, funding for 2025 can be received, and to demonstrate progress in on-chain governance — despite our significant reservations about the budget process... This vote is not a guarantee of future support should the budgeting and withdrawal process be repeated in future cycles without improvement.
section_9_notable_quotes.significance: Sets explicit conditions for future support, demonstrating CF's increasingly active governance role

section_9_notable_quotes.quote: Cardano's fixed supply and disinflationary emission schedule are not mere marketing points—they are pillars of our network's integrity and competitive advantage. Unlike traditional fiscal budgeting, treasury disbursements on Cardano must be approached as a form of monetary policy intervention, with profound implications for inflation and token value.
section_9_notable_quotes.significance: Frames treasury governance as monetary policy — the strongest economic framing in the dataset

section_9_notable_quotes.quote: Intersect has been greatly shaped into a leaner and meaner machine by pushback, not by support. Fortunately, there were sufficient NOs and ABSTAINS to create enough pushback... I want to reciprocate with my own leap of faith, by supporting a key cog in the system — the new community-minded Intersect. In this space, all we have the power to do is really to make a decision when and if to trust someone.
section_9_notable_quotes.significance: Illustrates how DRep NO votes serve as reform pressure rather than just blocking — a governance insight

section_9_notable_quotes.quote: This is not a spend by the treasury, this is a managed fund that has the potential to also generate returns for the treasury, making it inherently an EV-positive play (minus risk). I hope that this proposal can finally be put forward after being stymied multiple times by governance drama and technicalities.
section_9_notable_quotes.significance: The clearest articulation of the pro-DeFi-liquidity case: treasury as investment capital, not expenditure

section_9_notable_quotes.proposal: Cardano Global Listing Expansion - Powered by Snek
section_9_notable_quotes.quote: Treasury allocations for exchange listings should be tied to clear, measurable benefits for the broader ecosystem, either through collective infrastructure, demonstrable long-term ROI, or repayment to the Treasury. In its current form, this proposal focuses on a single-token listing without such mechanisms in place, creating a precedent that may be difficult to sustain.
section_9_notable_quotes.significance: Defines the principled case against single-token exchange listing funding from a major DRep

section_9_notable_quotes.quote: 97 million ADA for what reads like a university research department's wishlist... pick three things and do them excellently instead of promising everything to everyone. In the age of Voltaire, the community deserves better than 'trust us, we're the smart guys.' I mean, of course you are, but at least show me?
section_9_notable_quotes.significance: Articulates the accountability expectation for even the most trusted technical teams

section_9_notable_quotes.quote: EBITDA is an accounting outcome, not a constitutional safeguard. It depends on future operations, future market adoption, future cost allocations, and future management choices. Don't confuse contingent upside with hard accountability. If the core proposal does not justify the withdrawal on its own merits, a back-ended revenue-sharing promise does not rescue it! Again: Hope is not a strategy!
section_9_notable_quotes.significance: The most sophisticated critique of revenue-share DeFi models — financial due diligence applied to governance

founding_entity_dynamics.summary: A persistent undercurrent of frustration with EMURGO and Cardano Foundation using community treasury while retaining genesis ADA governance power
founding_entity_dynamics.gaia_thesis: Founding entities should burn genesis ADA for ecosystem operations rather than tapping community treasury — expressed on Critical Integrations, Summit 2026, and multiple other proposals
founding_entity_dynamics.emurgo_governance_concern: InputEndorsers has a standing NO vote on EMURGO proposals until March 2027 due to Yoroi wallet UI issue that directed users to delegate DRep power to EMURGO
founding_entity_dynamics.cf_improving_trust: CF's adoption of a published evaluation framework and explicit abstentions on IO proposals where they had criticism signals more professional governance behavior
founding_entity_dynamics.gaia_estimate: EMURGO controls ~16% of all governance voting power through EMURGO + YOROI; CF controls ~4.22%

defi_vs_infrastructure_divide.summary: The sharpest ideological split in treasury governance: DeFi-supporting DReps (Cerkoryn, GAIA in specific cases, HOSKY, Eternl, etc.) vs infrastructure-purists (TriangleForces, InputEndorsers in some contexts, GAIA in others)
defi_vs_infrastructure_divide.cerkoryn_position: Open-minded to DeFi as EV-positive investment if returns flow back to treasury; skeptical of amounts
defi_vs_infrastructure_divide.gaia_position: Against DeFi from treasury on principle; DeFi is commercial and must be self-sustaining; but supports stablecoin/liquidity infrastructure
